title: Phase-Contrast MRI for Hemodynamical Changes in Cerebral Aneurysms
author: Philipp Arnold
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kekctcw

steps.title: Prepare Experimental Fluid
steps.instruction: Prepare a 58% aqueous glycerol mixture to serve as the Newtonian experimental fluid.

substeps.instruction: Test the mixture of the two components with a refractometer before each MRI run to ensure comparable results.

steps.title: Set Up Flow Circuit and Phantom
steps.instruction: Establish a closed-circuit flow system using a computer-controlled piston pump and silicone tubes to drive the experimental fluid through aneurysm phantoms.

substeps.instruction: Place aneurysm phantoms inside a hand wrist coil of a 3T Philips Ingenia MRI scanner to maximize spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Connect a flow meter and two pressure sensors (positioned before and after the aneurysm phantom) to monitor flow and pressure patterns.
Start the piston pump and allow it to reach a stable flow of approximately 160 ml/min with physiological systolic and diastolic pressures of approximately 140/80 mmHg.
Synchronize the MRI to the piston pump using a photo diode connected to the pump as an external trigger.

steps.title: Acquire Phase-Contrast MRI Data
steps.instruction: Perform image acquisition using a 4D phase contrast multi-shot 3D Gradient-Echo sequence (turbo-factor 5, without SENSE).

substeps.instruction: Set acquisition parameters: TE = 2.9 ms, TR = 6.1 ms, alpha = 10°.
Set velocity encoding level (VENC) to 100 cm/s for each spatial direction to prevent aliasing in the aneurysm region.
Acquire flow in all three spatial directions (ap, rl, cc) consecutively in a single scan.
Ensure the total scan duration is 30:44 min.
Maintain spatial resolution of RLxAPxFH = 0.53x0.53x0.60 mm³ with a matrix size of 112x112x94 voxels and a temporal resolution of 71 ms.

steps.title: Reconstruct Velocity Field and Process Data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired MRI data to reconstruct the quantitative velocity field and vessel anatomy.

substeps.instruction: Correct the quantitative velocity field for magnetic field inhomogeneities using static measurements.
Save MRI data as DICOM files containing magnitude and phase-contrast information for all three directions (FH, AP, RL).
Import DICOM files into MATLAB using the dicomread function.
Perform threshold-based semi-automatic segmentation of the magnitude data slice by slice, with correction by an experienced physician, to reconstruct vessel anatomy.
Set voxels outside the reconstructed vessel anatomy to have no flow in any direction.
